title: Gravel Calculator
metaTitle: Gravel Calculator: How Much Gravel or Stone You Need
metaDescription: Calculate cubic yards and tons of gravel for driveways, patios, and landscaping. Adjust depth and stone density to match your material.

constants.label: Density (tons per cubic yard)
constants.note: Typical crushed stone. Pea gravel is lighter (~1.3), dense stone is heavier (~1.5). Check with your supplier.

content.intro: Gravel is sold by the ton or by the cubic yard, so knowing your volume before you call the quarry or home center keeps you from running short or paying for extra delivery trips. This calculator takes the dimensions of your project area and the depth of stone you need, then gives you cubic yards and estimated tons. The default density of 1.4 tons per cubic yard suits most crushed stone; adjust it for lighter pea gravel or heavier granite. Measure your area, enter the numbers below, and get a reliable estimate to place your order. Results are estimates — confirm with your supplier before you buy.
content.howItWorks: The formula multiplies length × width × depth (depth converted from inches to feet) to find cubic feet, then divides by 27 for cubic yards. Tons needed = cubic yards × (1 + waste%) × density. Formula: cubic feet = L × W × (D ÷ 12). Cubic yards = cubic feet ÷ 27. Tons = cubic yards × (1 + waste%) × density.

examples.title: A 20 by 10 foot driveway section at 4 inches deep
examples.text: Length 20 ft, width 10 ft, depth 4 in. Cubic feet = 20 × 10 × (4 ÷ 12) = 66.67 ft³. Cubic yards = 66.67 ÷ 27 = 2.47 yd³. With 10% waste and 1.4 tons per cubic yard: tons = 2.47 × 1.1 × 1.4 = 3.80 tons.

commonMistakes: Measuring depth in feet instead of inches — 4 inches is 0.33 feet, not 4.
Using an average density without confirming the specific stone type with the quarry.
Ordering by weight without checking whether the supplier weighs wet or dry material.
Forgetting extra material for settling and compaction into the soil sub-base.

faq.q: How deep should gravel be for a driveway?
faq.a: A driveway typically needs 4 to 6 inches of compacted crushed stone. For walking paths and patio borders, 2 to 3 inches is usually plenty.

faq.q: How much does one cubic yard of gravel weigh?
faq.a: Most crushed stone weighs between 1.3 and 1.5 tons per cubic yard. Coarser gravel is on the heavier end; dry pea gravel is slightly lighter.

faq.q: How many tons of gravel are in a dump truck load?
faq.a: A standard tri-axle dump truck can carry 10 to 14 tons of gravel, while a single-axle truck usually carries 4 to 6 tons.

faq.q: Why do I need a waste factor?
faq.a: Gravel compacts when driven on and shifts into uneven ground. A 10% waste buffer ensures you have enough stone to reach full depth.
